extracted.intended_audience: telecommunications carriers, parties filing international/telecommunications applications with the FCC, and applicants/participants in FCC competitive bidding
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing electronic filing via the International Bureau Filing System (ICFS), post-filing processing, special/emergency filings, and Communications Assistance for Law Enforcement Act (CALEA) obligations for telecommunications carriers, plus application requirements for competitive bidding for universal service support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment requirements for electronic applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Many applications require exhibits or attachments. If attachments are required, you must attach documentation to your electronic application before filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted attachment formats: Word, Adobe Acrobat, Excel and Text.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICFS file numbers are administrative only
rubrics_metrics.description: We assign file numbers to electronic applications in order to facilitate processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We only assign file numbers for administrative convenience; they do not mean that an application is acceptable for filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRN registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must register for an FCC Registration Number (FRN) to process electronic applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you already have an FRN, use it. You may obtain an FRN from CORES or through ICFS as part of the filing process. Applicants, transferees/assignees, transferors/assignors, licensees/authorization holders, or payers are required to have and use an FRN when filing and/or paying fees through ICFS. The FRN is used to give secured access to ICFS and to pre-fill the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICFS account registration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to complete and file your electronic application, you must register in ICFS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can register in your name, your company's name, or your client's name. ICFS will issue an account number and you create your own password. For forgotten passwords contact icfsinfo@fcc.gov or (202) 418-2222.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete application data and required information
rubrics_metrics.description: You must completely fill out forms and provide all requested information as provided in parts 1, 25, 63, and 64 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must provide a U.S. Postal Service mail delivery address (email is encouraged). Answer questions calling for specific technical data or yes/no/short answers. You may incorporate by reference lengthy showings already on file only if: (i) the referenced information is filed in ICFS; (ii) the referenced information is current and accurate in all material respects; and (iii) the application identifies where the referenced information can be found (application file number if to prior applications, or title of proceeding, docket number, and legal citation if to a docketed proceeding).

rubrics_metrics.name: File confirmation and proof of filing
rubrics_metrics.description: If you file your application successfully through ICFS, a confirmation screen will appear showing the date/time of filing and your submission ID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Print this verification for your records as proof of online filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee payment requirement and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Most applications require that you pay a fee before the Commission can begin processing your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine fee via § 1.1107, the International and Satellite Services fee guide, or by running a draft electronic submission of payment online form through ICFS. You must electronically submit payment within fourteen (14) calendar days of the date you file your application in ICFS or we will dismiss your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCC electronic submission of payment online form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete FCC electronic submission of payment online form must accompany all fee payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the FRN for both the applicant and the payer and include your submission ID number in the box labeled “FCC Code 2.” For transfer/assignment applications, enter involved call signs in “FCC Code 1.” You can generate a pre-filled form from ICFS using your IB submission ID. Payment options: credit card (through ICFS), online ACH, or wire/other electronic payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic record is the official record (no paper copies required)
rubrics_metrics.description: When you file electronically through ICFS, the electronic record is the official record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You do not need to submit paper copies of your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic signature and retention of signed originals
rubrics_metrics.description: An electronic application is 'signed' when there is an electronic signature (the typed name of the person signing, electronically transmitted via ICFS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For all electronically filed applications, you (or the signor) must actually sign a paper copy of the application and keep the signed original in your files. Only original applications, amendments, and related statements of fact need be signed. Who signs: individuals sign if they are an individual; one partner for partnerships; officer/director/authorized employee for corporations; an officer-member for unauthorized associations. Attorneys may sign on behalf of a physically disabled or absent filer but must explain why the filer is not signing and must explain reasons for any statements made solely on belief. Signing under oath is unnecessary, but willful false statements are punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001 and by administrative sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICFS system availability
rubrics_metrics.description: ICFS is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week for filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking application status
rubrics_metrics.description: You can check the status of your application through the 'Search Tools' on the ICFS homepage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICFS homepage located at https://www.fcc.gov/icfs

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial review, dismissal, and requests for additional information
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing, the application is routed to an analyst for initial review. If the application is incomplete, we will either dismiss it or contact you to request additional information within a specified time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requested additional information is not received within the specified time, we will dismiss the application. Dismissals are without prejudice so you may refile a complete application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted for Filing Public Notice and comment period
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is complete and payment is verified, it will appear on an 'Accepted for Filing' Public Notice unless public notice is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An 'Accepted for Filing' Public Notice gives the public time to comment on the filing; the comment period varies depending on the type of application. Certain applications (e.g., some pro forma notifications) do not have to go on an 'Accepted for Filing' Public Notice prior to initiation of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-public-notice review and possible coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Public Notice, your application may undergo legal, technical and/or financial review and may require coordination with other government agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After review, the Commission will decide to grant, deny, or take other action; grants/denials/actions are noted in the ICFS database. Some filings may be granted automatically on a specific date unless notified otherwise prior to that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorizations and notices issued for different application types
rubrics_metrics.description: Different types of applications result in different forms of authorization documents or Public Notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: certain actions use 'Action Taken' Public Notices with specific report number formats (e.g., SAT-xxxxx for satellite space station), some filings yield mailed licenses or letters, others result in Commission Orders or Form A-732 for transfers, and streamlined Section 214 applications' Action Taken Public Notice can serve as the authorization document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions for emergency filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes licenses, modifications or renewals may be granted even if no one files an application when emergency circumstances exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: emergencies involving danger to life/property or equipment damage; national emergency proclaimed by President or Congress; during a war when grants are necessary for national defense; or when it's not feasible to secure renewal applications. Emergency authorizations stop at the end of emergency periods; after the period, you must submit the appropriate form electronically. Procedures for emergency requests are specified in §§ 25.120 and 63.25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Temporary Authority (STA) filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for Special Temporary Authority may be filed via ICFS for most services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing via ICFS is encouraged to ensure faster receipt. For specific content requirements, refer to §§ 25.120 and 63.25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting additional information in response to official requests
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to an official request for information from the Space Bureau and Office of International Affairs, additional information can be submitted electronically to the requestor or by mail to the Office of the Secretary, Attention: Space Bureau or Office of International Affairs, as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If the service rules allow, you may amend pending applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an electronic version of an amendment application is available in ICFS, you may file your amendment electronically through ICFS.

rubrics_metrics.name: CALEA purpose: authorized activation and assistance capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Carriers must ensure that any interception of communications or access to call-identifying information effected within their switching premises can be activated only in accordance with appropriate legal authorization, appropriate carrier authorization, and with the affirmative intervention of an individual officer or employee; and implement the assistance capability requirements of CALEA section 103, 47 U.S.C. 1002.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for CALEA implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions to be used solely for the purpose of implementing CALEA requirements, including 'appropriate legal authorization', 'appropriate carrier authorization', 'appropriate authorization', 'LEA', and 'telecommunications carrier'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate legal authorization means a court order signed by a judge or magistrate authorizing interception, or other authorization pursuant to 18 U.S.C. 2518(7) or other relevant statute. Telecommunications carrier includes entities engaged in transmission or switching as common carriers, providers of commercial mobile service per 47 U.S.C. 332(d), or entities the Commission deems to be carriers replacing a substantial portion of local telephone exchange service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies and procedures for employee supervision and control (CALEA)
rubrics_metrics.description: A telecommunications carrier shall appoint a senior officer responsible for ensuring interceptions or access can be activated only with appropriate legal and carrier authorization and affirmative intervention, and establish policies/procedures to implement this requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies/procedures must include: (1) a statement that personnel must receive appropriate legal and carrier authorization before enabling interception or access; (2) an interpretation of 'appropriate authorization'; (3) a detailed description of record retention length per § 1.20004; and (4) a separate appendix with the name and job function of the senior officer and 24/7 contact information for CALEA points of contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting compromises and unlawful surveillance (CALEA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Carriers must report to affected law enforcement agencies, within a reasonable time upon discovery, any act of compromise of a lawful interception or access to call-identifying information to unauthorized persons or entities, and any act of unlawful electronic surveillance that occurred on their premises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining secure and accurate records of interceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A carrier shall maintain a secure and accurate record of each interception of communications or access to call-identifying information, made with or without appropriate authorization, in the form of a single certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification must include at minimum: telephone/circuit IDs involved; start date/time of interception; identity of the law enforcement officer presenting the authorization; name of the person signing the legal authorization; type of interception (e.g., pen register, trap and trace, Title III, FISA); and the name of the carrier personnel responsible for overseeing the interception. The certification must be signed by the responsible individual, compiled contemporaneously or within a reasonable period after initiation, and may be satisfied by signing the certification and appending the legal authorization and any extensions. Carriers must maintain these records for a reasonable period determined by the carrier and ensure records are complete and accurate. Violation subject to penalties in § 1.20008.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing CALEA policies/procedures with the Commission and Commission review
rubrics_metrics.description: Each telecommunications carrier shall file with the Commission the policies and procedures it uses to comply with this subpart before commencing service and thereafter within 90 days of a carrier's merger/divestiture or amendment of its policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will review policies/procedures for compliance with §§ 1.20003 and 1.20004 and may order modifications. As of June 29, 2023, filings required by this paragraph shall be submitted electronically through the CALEA Electronic Filing System (CEFS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance capability requirements and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Telecommunications carriers shall provide to a LEA the assistance capability requirements of CALEA regarding wire and electronic communications and call-identifying information (47 U.S.C. 1002).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A carrier may satisfy these requirements by complying with publicly available technical requirements or standards adopted by industry associations or by the Commission (e.g., J-STD-025 current version). Carriers shall consult with manufacturers and support service providers to ensure current and planned equipment, facilities, and services comply. Manufacturers/providers shall, on a reasonably timely basis and at a reasonable charge, make available features or modifications necessary to permit carriers to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional assistance capabilities for wireline, cellular, and PCS carriers
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to § 1.20006, wireline, cellular, and PCS carriers shall provide to a LEA the assistance capability requirements regarding wire and electronic communications and call-identifying information covered by J-STD-025 (current version), and may satisfy these by complying with J-STD-025 or by other means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These carriers also shall provide capabilities including: content of subject-initiated conference calls; party hold/join/drop on conference calls; subject-initiated dialing and signaling information; in-band and out-of-band signaling; timing information; and dialed digit extraction with a toggle feature to activate/deactivate this capability. Timing information: a call-identifying message must be sent from the carrier's IAP to the LEA's Collection Function within eight seconds of receipt at least 95% of the time, and timestamped to an accuracy of at least 200 milliseconds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for CALEA violations
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of a carrier's violation of this subchapter, the Commission shall enforce the penalties articulated in 47 U.S.C. 503(b) of the Communications Act of 1934 and 47 CFR 1.80.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of competitive bidding subpart
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart sets forth procedures for competitive bidding to determine recipients of universal service support pursuant to part 54 and the amount(s) of support each recipient may receive, subject to post-auction procedures, when the Commission directs determination through competitive bidding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice of application process for competitive bidding
rubrics_metrics.description: The dates and procedures for submitting applications to participate in competitive bidding pursuant to this subpart shall be announced by public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contents for participation in competitive bidding
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise established by public notice, an applicant shall provide in acceptable form: identity of the applicant and ownership information; identities of up to three individuals authorized to make or withdraw a bid; identities of real parties in interest and description of any agreements relating to participation; certifications regarding partnerships/joint ventures/agreements; and various certifications of non-collusion, internal controls, technical/marketplace capability, compliance with § 1.21002, statutory/regulatory compliance to receive support, and acceptance of potential default payments/forfeitures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific items: (1) identity and ownership per § 1.2112(a); (2) up to three authorized bidders (no person may be authorized bidder for more than one auction applicant); (3) identities of real parties in interest and brief description of related agreements; (4) certification describing and identifying each party to partnerships/jvs/consortia and any agreements relating to participation including communications about bids or strategies; (5) certification of no prohibited agreements addressing bidding or post-auction market structure; (6) certification of internal controls if applicant has interest in more than one application to prevent cross-information; (7) certification of applicant's sole responsibility to evaluate technical and market factors and ability to build/operate if awarded; (8) certification of compliance with § 1.21002; (9) certification of compliance with statutory/regulatory requirements to receive support (or acknowledgement compliance required before support); (10) certification of exposure to default payment/forfeiture and obligation to pay under § 1.21004.
